text: The chicken skeleton allows the bird to stand and protects internal organs and tissues. It is compact and lightweight but strong. The tail and neck vertebrae are movable, but the body vertebrae are not, which gives the body enough strength to support the wings. There are two special types of bone: pneumatic bones (empty bones connected to the chicken's air sacs, important for breathing — examples include the skull, humerus, clavicle, sternum, and some vertebrae) and medullary bones (an important source of calcium for the laying hen — examples include the tibia, femur, ribs, ulna, toes, and scapula).
